blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The northeast monsoon, or “amihan,” has weakened and is no longer affecting the country, the state weather bureau said on Saturday. In its 5 a.m. forecast, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) announced that it is the easterlies that continue to prevail, affecting the eastern portion of the country. “The northeast monsoon is not felt in our country, and the easterlies or the warm air from the Pacific Ocean is affecting our country,” Pagasa weather specialist Veronica Torres-Bagalanon reported.
